author: Andrew Newland
title: New INDOT data shows decrease in traffic accidents - NewsBreak
text:
By Andrew Newland Jared Darwish ,
2 hours ago
EVANSVILLEE, Ind. (WEHT) — New research indicates the intersection of Highway 41 and Washington Avenue is safer now after major changes.
INDOT says in the last six months, its data shows a significant decrease in accidents of all kinds, something officials credit to the improvements made to both the pedestrian areas and roadways.
“Putting a few signs up isn’t going to do completely what needs to be done, so we got the delineators up that’s helping show people that physically, you can’t make those left turns at the intersection, i think that has really helped,” INDOT Public Relations Director Gary Brian said.
INDOT’s data shows only one injury crash at the intersection since these improvements have been made. From 2016 to 2018 INDOT says the intersection averaged five severe incidents per year.
“When we started looking at this project for the pedestrian bridge, we were also looking at how we can help make the intersection itself safer right, because we don’t want to do a half job,” Brian said.
Brain says there have been no more than three incidents per month, with some months having zero since the project was finished.
“It is imperative to make these as safe as possible so everyone can get to their destination safely, and that is why we do this job.”
Although this is one of INDOT’s newest projects in the state in terms of traffic prevention, they say they are still looking for ways to improve this intersection and make it safer, of course they say they can’t do that without recommendations and suggestions from the public.
